answer: Trickle-Entry Rate Cap. Each identity must complete its first N actions across randomized, sparse windows; bursts are throttled at a mesa-sized ceiling per interval. An attacker farming accounts hits the dune of queued actions and must pay idle capacity rent plus delayed payoff per identity, since each yarrow-thin account waits out windows independently. Duplicates thus forfeit fast returns and absorb the full cost of staggered dormancy.
